column2: DEFER severity=MED — mobile/__tests__/lotMapPage.behaviour.test.tsx:70 "const s = buildLotMapSituation({ query: i.query, data: i.data as never, error: null, isFetching: i.isFetching ?? false, schemaDrift: false, selectedParcelId: i.selectedParcelId ?? null });" — the it.each list names error, rate_limited, unauthorized and schema_drift, but every case is built with error null and schemaDrift false, so those four lists render as ordinary trees and the declared Input field error (line 52) is never read anywhere in the file — build with error: err(i.error) and schemaDrift: i.error === 'schema_drift' (the errorOf construction in lotMapScreens.golden.test.ts), or drop those four names from the list

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/daylightSearchPages.golden.test.ts:45 "for (const [table, o] of Object.entries({ PARCEL_SEARCH_LAYOUT, LOT_MAP_LAYOUT }) as Array<[string, Record<string, string>]>) {" — the unchecked cast promises every table value is a string and line 46 feeds it to classTokens(v).split, so any numeric or nested entry (the sibling style table carries numbers, pageTable.logic.test.ts:20 "bottomPadding: 7, maxWidth: 9, backIconSize: 3") throws a TypeError instead of reporting a bad token — take the value as unknown and guard typeof v === 'string' before splitting, skipping the rest

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/daylightSearchPages.golden.test.ts:22 "type Json = Record<string, any>; // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- fixture JSON" — typing the parsed fixtures as Record<string, any> makes every builder call in this file unchecked (i.query, i.data, i.selected at lines 32 and 33 are any, so a renamed or dropped fixture field compiles silently) — use Record<string, unknown> and an explicit Input type as lotMapScreens.golden.test.ts:24 "type Input = { query: string; data?: ConsumerParcelLookupResult; ... }" does

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/parcelScreens.golden.test.ts:168 "const order = ids(at('rate_limited_zero')).filter((x) => /ratelimit|error|retry|candidate|refine|empty|prompt/.test(x));" — the test title promises the block order "notices, list, refine, miss, prompt" but rate_limited_zero carries no candidates, refine, miss or prompt, so only the three notice ids are ordered and the list/refine/miss/prompt order named in the title is never asserted — assert the order on the ambiguous tree (which has candidates and refine) or rename the test to what it checks

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/lotMapPage.behaviour.test.tsx:71 "render(<SurfaceRenderer tree={lotMapProps(s) as never} content={LOT_MAP_SLICE.content} data={lotMapData(s)} actions={actions()} />);" — as never is used four times in this file (tree here, data at lines 70 and 76/82), which silences every prop and data type check the render smoke exists to exercise, so a tree shape SurfaceRenderer cannot consume would compile and fail only at render — type the tree prop as the shared PropsNode both bindings return and pass it without the cast

DEFER severity=MED — src/lib/parcels/consumer-lookup.ts "  if (v == null) return null;" — `Number('')` is 0, so a blank numeric value (for example a comparable `build_ratio` or `permit_fsi`) is emitted as 0 rather than null, while the sibling `lot-map.ts` `num` returns null for `''` (see `(v == null || v === '' || !Number.isFinite(Number(v)) ? null : Number(v))`) — add `|| v === ''` to the guard so blank values stay null.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/lib/parcels/lot-map.ts "  if (outline !== null && outline.length > OUTLINE_MAX_BYTES) {" — `.length` is UTF-16 code units, not bytes, so the constant named `OUTLINE_MAX_BYTES` is compared against a character count; a multi-byte GeoJSON body can exceed the intended byte cap unnoticed — rename to `OUTLINE_MAX_CHARS` or compute `Buffer.byteLength(outline)`.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/lib/parcels/geometry.ts "  const n = ring.length - 1; // exclude closing point" — `shoelaceArea` and `minimumBoundingRect` always drop the final vertex without checking `last === first`, whereas `computeCentroid` explicitly handles an unclosed ring, so a ring that is not closed silently loses one real vertex here — mirror the `computeCentroid` check (`last[0] === first[0] && last[1] === first[1] ? n-1 : n`) in both functions.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/lib/parcels/lot-size-entry.ts "export const VERIFIED_LOT_AREA_SOURCES: readonly string[] = [];" — because the array is empty, the `effectiveLotSize` verified branch (`VERIFIED_LOT_AREA_SOURCES.includes(read.city_source)`) can never be true, so that precedence step is dead code until a source is added — remove the branch or add a test/lint lock that fails once a source is declared so the branch is exercised.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/lib/parcels/lot-size-entry.ts "resultsInputStamp === read.entry!.entered_at.toISOString()" — the non-null assertion hides `read.entry` nullability, and it is only safe because of the preceding `entered` boolean, not because TypeScript narrowed it — narrow inline (`read.entry !== null && ... read.entry.entered_at.toISOString()`) instead of asserting.
BUG severity=<none> — cannot see? No CRIT/HIGH found. Provide the mandated form only.
BUG severity=CRIT — none found
BUG severity=HIGH — none found

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/customer-report-compute.logic.test.ts:46 "const m = cr(`${process.cwd()}/package.json`)(`${process.cwd()}/scripts/lib/compute/compute-maxbld-scenarios.js`) as Record<string, unknown>;" — the core mock resolves through process.cwd() while the same file pins "const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');" on :25, so a run from any other directory throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND inside the vi.mock factory instead of a readable failure — resolve the two paths from ROOT (and CORE_REL) in the factory.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/customer-report-compute.logic.test.ts:47 "h.loaded.core += 1;" — the counters increment only on the first evaluation of each mock factory, so once any earlier test has loaded the core the C1 assertion "expect(h.loaded.core).toBe(coreBefore);" can no longer detect an import before the gate (vitest --sequence.shuffle makes it vacuous) — reset the module registry before the C1 case or assert on a per-import spy (vi.mocked on the lazy import) rather than a one-shot load counter.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/parcel-lookup-gate.infra.test.ts:120 "const realAssemble = vi.mocked(assembleConsumerPayload).getMockImplementation()!;" — an unchecked non-null assertion captured at module scope; if the factory's vi.fn(a.assembleConsumerPayload) is ever changed every "real assembler" case throws "realAssemble is not a function" inside a mock with no hint of the cause — assert typeof realAssemble === 'function' at capture, or throw a named Error there.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/parcel-lookup-gate.infra.test.ts:306 "vi.mocked(assembleConsumerPayload).mockImplementation(realAssemble as never);" — the as never cast erases the whole mock signature, so a change to the route's call signature or the assembler's parameters still compiles and only fails at runtime — drop the cast (realAssemble already has the mock's type) or type it as Parameters<typeof assembleConsumerPayload>.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/fix-tune.logic.test.ts:62 "expect(code('mobile/src/lib/semiQuestion.ts')).toMatch(/sliceNumber\(slice, 'continue_wait_ms'\)/);" — the case is titled "both phone read sites use the one reader" but asserts only semiQuestion.ts, and the hook half is already asserted one case above, so this test adds no coverage while its name claims a second site — either add the HOOK assertion here (sliceNumber(searchSlice, ...) over KEYS) or retitle it to the one site it checks.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/link-massing.infra.test.ts:63 "expect(declared[name]!.min, `${name} declares no lower bound`).toBe(SEED[name]!.min);" — SEED[name] carries a non-null assertion this test never proves, so a seed key dropped later surfaces as "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'min')" instead of naming the variable — replumb through the same `if (!entry) throw new Error(...)` guard the three cases above use.

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/surfaces/nav-by-route.logic.test.ts "const jsxBranch = (ts.isBinaryExpression(p) && p.operatorToken.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.AmpersandAmpersandToken && hasJsx(p.right))" — when the state comparison is only an operand of a conjunction (`if (a && view === 'b') return <jsx>` or `if (view === 'b' && a)`), unparen returns the `&&` node whose right is not JSX, so the state is never marked a discriminant and NAV-1 misses a real state-as-route violation, the lock passing it silently — also mark the discriminant when the comparison sits as an operand of a `&&`/`||`/ternary whose other branch carries JSX, or inspect the enclosing statement rather than only the immediate parent.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/parcel-legacy-oracle.logic.test.ts "const contentForms = new Set(Object.values(content).map((v) => v.replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, '{}')));" — fill() substitutes a config key with its value ("3") while contentForms only collapses the placeholder to "{}", so a legacy attribute that references {SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LEN} can only match if the content file bakes the number rather than the documented placeholder, contradicting the comment "placeholders filled with the config values" — apply fill() (or the same placeholder normalization on both sides) so a config-placeholder content string matches.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/parcel-legacy-oracle.logic.test.ts "const goldenTestIDs = [...goldenStrings].filter((s) => s.startsWith('parcel-'));" — this treats every string literal prop beginning with "parcel-" (a route, a label) as a testID, so a dropped/renamed testID can be "found" by an unrelated literal and the oracle passes wrongly — collect testIDs from props whose key is testID rather than from all literal values.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/page-arm.logic.test.ts "const sec = (s: Json, id: string): Json => s.sections.find((x: Json) => x.id === id);" — the return type hides that find() can return undefined, so a wrong section id surfaces as a TypeError on the following `.when = v` assignment instead of a clear assertion — return `Json | undefined` or throw with the missing id.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/surfaces/page-arm.logic.test.ts "const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'page-arm-'));" — these temp trees are never removed (no afterAll), leaking directories across runs, unlike the neighbour nav-by-route.logic.test.ts which removes its tmpRoot in afterAll — add an afterAll that rm's the created roots.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/surfaces/register-locks-resolve.infra.test.ts "expect(r.status).toBe(0);" — trackedSet() runs this expect at module import via "const TRACKED = trackedSet();", so a missing/failing git turns the whole file into a collection-time error rather than a per-test diagnostic — hoist the git call into a beforeAll and fail the specific test with the git stderr.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/search-web-binding.ui.test.tsx:46 "const textsOf = (n: unknown, s: WebSituation): string[] => {" — the second parameter `s` is threaded through both recursive calls and never read anywhere in the body, so it is a dead parameter — drop it and pass only the node at the two call sites.

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/surfaces/static-page.logic.test.ts:151 "filter((l) => /^\s*import\b/.test(l) && /require-parcel-tool-page|requireParcelToolPage/.test(l))" — the guard only sees an import whose module path or named binding sits on the same line as `import`, so a wrapped `import {\n  requireParcelToolPage,\n} from '@/lib/auth/require-parcel-tool-page';` is invisible and T5 passes with the gate present — match the identifier over the whole file text (comments stripped) instead of line by line.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/surface-conformance.logic.test.ts:1052 "JSON.stringify(p).includes('\"integer\"')" — a config property declared `\"number\"` is filtered out of `numberKeys`, so the check titled "every number-typed property a config may hold has its rule" silently skips it — accept both `\"integer\"` and `\"number\"` in the filter.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/surface-validate.logic.test.ts:352 "expect(r.lines.every((l) => l.startsWith('SV-'))).toBe(true);" — `every` on an empty array is true, so a run that exits 1 while printing nothing to stderr satisfies the "no stack trace, only SV lines" assertion vacuously — also assert the line list is non-empty.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/surfaces/surface-conformance.logic.test.ts:1017 "expect([k, r.default, r.min, r.max, r.type]).toEqual([k, ...(want[k] as [number, number, number]), 'number'].flat());" — `.flat()` on an already flat array literal is a no-op that reads as if it did something — delete it.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/surfaces/search-web-binding.ui.test.tsx:41 "if (!CONSOLE_ALLOW.some((r) => r.test(m))) errors.push(m);" — the collected `errors` array is asserted only inside describe (a); a console error raised by the interaction renders in (b), (c) and (e) is swallowed with no assertion at all — assert `errors` is empty in the `afterEach` so every case is covered.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/reportScreens.golden.test.ts:259 "const g = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), '..', 'src/tests/fixtures/report-page', `${st}.mobile.json`), 'utf8'));" — this one path is anchored on process.cwd() while the same file computes REPO at line 20 ("const REPO = path.resolve(MOBILE, '..');"), so the case only resolves when jest is invoked from mobile/ and throws ENOENT anywhere else — read path.join(REPO, 'src/tests/fixtures/report-page', `${st}.mobile.json`) like every other read in the file.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/reportScreen.mount.behaviour.test.tsx:133 "expect(mockSemi.every((v) => v === undefined)).toBe(true);" — after "mockSemi.length = 0;" the assertion is vacuously true when the second render never calls the hook, so the "no semi param means undefined" lock can pass without the hook being called at all — assert on a non-empty array, e.g. expect(mockSemi).toEqual([undefined]) behind a length check.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/semiQuestionScreens.golden.test.ts:66 "const checked = radios.filter((n) => (n.props.accessibilityState as Json).checked === true);" — the cast hides that accessibilityState may be absent, so a binding that stops emitting it makes the helper throw "Cannot read properties of undefined" instead of producing the problem line the helper exists for — read (n.props.accessibilityState as Json | undefined)?.checked === true and emit a problem when the key is missing.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/__tests__/reportScreens.golden.test.ts:53 "const p = v.sections.find((s) => s.id === id)?.parts[at as unknown as number];" — the double cast makes a malformed part ref ("o1.title", "o1.") index undefined, so the pending-style check silently passes for exactly the refs it exists to police — parse the index and push a problem when it is not an integer inside parts.length.

DEFER severity=MED — mobile/src/components/surfaces/SurfaceRenderer.tsx:119 "return () => act.select(String(resolveValue(a.parcelId, ctx)));" — action arguments are stringified with no missing-value guard, and PageTableBinding writes the argument under the row's own name ("onPress: { action: s.action, [s.arg]: { derived: `${s.id}.${i}` } }"), so a select row whose arg is not exactly parcelledId reaches the screen as the literal string "undefined" with no throw, silently dropping the tap — resolve the argument by the row's declared name and throw when it resolves to undefined, as resolveValue does for refs.

DEFER severity=MED — mobile/src/components/surfaces/LotMapBinding.tsx:179 "const lot = s.map!.lots[i]!;" — cards() dereferences the nullable map with non-null assertions while mapView() treats the same field as nullable ("const plain = s.map?.lots[i]?.hasFootprint === true"), so a multi_parcel situation whose map block is absent crashes the render instead of failing closed — guard s.map in cards (return [] or the unlinked notice) or read lots from s.map?.lots ?? [].

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/app/(app)/parcel-tool/semi-question.tsx:59 "let result;" — an uninitialised let is implicit any, so storeLookup(id, result) accepts anything, including a resolved undefined, with no type error — type it as the awaited return of answeredParcelLookup or restructure so the awaited value is const.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/app/(app)/parcel-tool/semi-question.tsx:63 "if (mountedRef.current) setSubmitError(e);" — the caught answered-lookup failure is never logged (no captureException, unlike the lookup hooks) and is discarded entirely when the page unmounted during the fetch — capture the exception before the mounted check, then set state only when mounted.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/src/components/surfaces/SurfaceRenderer.tsx:147 "const DATA_PROPS = new Set(['key', 'navigate']);" — navigate is written into every tree ("...(s.route ? { navigate: s.route } : {})") and skipped here, and every mount reads the situation field instead ("const route = situation.route;"), so within this material the tree prop is write-only — drop it from the bindings and goldens or have the mounts read tree.props.navigate.

DEFER severity=MED — mobile/src/lib/schemas.ts:427 "  .strict();" — the new lotForm block is strict while the file's own rule two screens up says "the map objects are plain (not .strict()), so a server-added field never raises ParcelLookupSchemaError on an installed build", so any additive key the server puts on lotForm now throws on the report page and lands it on the ErrorBoundary, which is the LOW-9 class this file says it fixed — fix: drop .strict() and leave the object plain like ParcelLotMapSchema and ParcelToolEntitlementSchema

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/src/lib/lotForm.ts:46 "export function lotFormEffective(detected: LotForm, override: LotForm | null | undefined): LotForm {" — no caller exists, the module header at line 9 states "nothing outside this file reads the param or calls `lotFormEffective` (P5.7)", so the diff adds an exported dead function — fix: drop it until 7.25 wires it, or keep it only with a unit test that pins it

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile/src/hooks/useParcelLookup.ts:105 "queryFn: () => fetchParcelLookup(parcelLookupParams(parcelId!, semi))," — the non-null assertion only holds while `enabled` blocks automatic fetching, a manual refetch on the disabled query runs this line with `parcelId` undefined and sends `parcelId=undefined` to the route — fix: make queryFn throw on a missing id, or type the key so the undefined case cannot reach the template

DEFER severity=NIT — mobile/src/lib/lotMap.ts:120 "errors: error != null ? errors : { ...errors, unexpected: false }," — the else branch is dead, `classifyParcelSearchError(null, ...)` at line 87 already returns `unexpected: false` because it is computed as `error != null && ...`, so the copy changes nothing (same line copied in semiQuestion.ts) — fix: return `errors,` directly in both files

DEFER severity=NIT — mobile/src/constants/lotMap.ts:86 "export const LOT_MAP_BOTTOM_PADDING = PARCEL_SHELF_HEIGHT + 24;" — the comment says "as the search page" but this re-derives SEARCH_BOTTOM_PADDING with a second copy of the literal 24 that PARCEL_SHELF_MIN_BOTTOM_PAD already names, so the two flow pages' bottom padding can drift silently — fix: import SEARCH_BOTTOM_PADDING from parcelSearch.ts

DEFER severity=NIT — mobile/src/hooks/useParcelLookup.ts:74 " * Debounced typeahead search. Fires when the trimmed query is ≥ 3 chars (the server min)." — the minimum is now read from the slice at line 83 (LOOKUP_MIN_QUERY_LEN), so the "3" in the doc is a second unchecked copy of a config value — fix: say "the slice's min_query_len"

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/lot-map-data-check.mjs:70 "await client.query('ROLLBACK');" — the ROLLBACK runs only when the SELECT resolves, so on a query error the BEGIN READ ONLY transaction is left to be discarded by client.end() rather than rolled back as the header at line 12 promises ("BEGIN READ ONLY, one SELECT, rolled back") — fix: issue the ROLLBACK from a catch/finally around the query so both paths roll back.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/surfaces/_schema/census/mobile-product.json:8048 "The six page settings of the phone search and semi pages are REGISTERED logic variables" — the sentence names six settings but enumerates five (debounce_ms, min_query_len, entitlement_stale_ms, lookup_retry_max, lookup_stale_ms) and says they are "declared here in config.logic_variables", where config.logic_variables holds exactly those five; the sixth (maxbld_page_continue_wait_ms) is declared in the semi-question entry, so "here" is wrong for one of the six — fix: say five settings are declared here and point the sixth at the semi-question entry.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/surfaces/_schema/census/contracts.json:23217 "surfaces": [ "mobile/src/hooks/useParcelLookup.ts:162" ] — the sharing surfaces list repeats the same file:line already carried by evidence and consumers_verified, while the sibling surface entry records the consumer as a surface via contract_ref (mobile-product.json "/api/parcels/entitlement"); a hook file path is not the surface the answer "sole" is describing — fix: name the consuming surface (mobile_parcel_search) or empty the list and keep the file:line only in evidence.

DEFER severity=NIT — scripts/surfaces/_schema/census/contracts.json:22902 "the route sends seven, src/app/api/parcels/entitlement/types.ts:12-18" — the same schema is cited as "src/app/api/parcels/entitlement/types.ts:10-19" in the check why at 23108, so one of the two ranges in this change is stale — fix: confirm the range and use it in both places.

DEFER severity=NIT — scripts/analysis/lot-map-data-check.mjs:80 "console.error(`error: ${e.message}`)" — the only log of a connect/query failure drops the stack, so a TypeError raised in main (for example the uncaught decodeURIComponent URIError on line 64) prints a bare message with no frame — fix: log the error object or e.stack as well.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/surfaces/emit-mobile-surfaces.mjs `if (!(entry.on_invalid === 'fail' || entry.on_invalid === 'clamp')) { problems.push(...)` — the function doc promises a problem line for "an entry whose min, max or on_invalid differs from the row", but the code only checks fail|clamp and never reads `row.on_invalid`, so a descriptor can flip a seed row's stated failure behaviour from fail to clamp and still generate — compare `entry.on_invalid !== row.on_invalid` and push that mismatch like min and max.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/surfaces/emit-mobile-surfaces.mjs `lines.push(\`GEN-STRAY ${dir}/${f}\`);` — `--check` reports stray generated files but the write branch `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(REPO, rel), t);` only writes, never deletes, so after a surface is renamed or dropped the check stays red with no in-tool remedy — have `--write` unlink files under SLICE_DIR and GOLDEN_COPY_DIR that `buildOutputs` no longer produces.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/surfaces/emit-mobile-surfaces.mjs `if (v < row.min || v > row.max) { problems.push(...)` — the line above already forces `v === row.default`, so this range check can only fire from a seed row whose default sits outside its own bounds, yet the message blames the descriptor value "is outside its bounds" — validate the row default against min/max when the row is read and drop this duplicate check, or reword the message.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/surfaces/_schema/static-page.schema.json screen_choices `"content": { "$ref": "#/$defs/id" }` — every sibling section types content as `#/$defs/contentKey` and every pasted content key is dotted (`map.clear.label`, `select.lot`), so a bare name here passes AJV and can never resolve to a leaf: the build-time leaf check the $comment promises cannot catch it — use `#/$defs/contentKey`.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/surfaces/_schema/static-page.schema.json `"A price part is followed in its box by its per and tax parts (drip pricing, s.74.01(1.1))."` — `plans.parts` is a flat array with no box grouping and no sequence constraint, so a box with a price and no tax, or per before price, validates cleanly — either encode the per-box rule or state in the comment that ordering is the binding's job and not checked here.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/surfaces/emit-mobile-surfaces.mjs `const life = rj(root, PRESENTATION).states.lifecycle;` — `lifecycle` is dereferenced with no check, so a rename of that key in report-presentation.json throws "Cannot convert undefined or null to object" from `Object.entries`, naming no file — guard it and throw `emit-mobile-surfaces: report-presentation.json states.lifecycle is missing`.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/surfaces/emit-mobile-surfaces.mjs report loop `const slice = { surface: id, config: {}, content };` then `out.set(\`${SLICE_DIR}/${id}.json\`, ...)` — nothing keeps the manifest's `converted` and `report` lists disjoint, so an id in both silently replaces the converted slice (config, bounds, page) and leaves an orphan goldens copy — assert the two lists do not intersect before building.

DEFER severity=NIT — scripts/surfaces/_schema/static-page.schema.json screen_bar `"platforms": { "type": "array", "minItems": 1, "uniqueItems": true, ... "enum": ["web","mobile"] }` — the identical array schema is repeated in screen, screen_bar, screen_status, screen_text, screen_notice, screen_choices and screen_button while flag, icon, action and contentKey already live in `$defs` — add one `$defs/platforms` and reference it.

BUG severity=HIGH — mobile_parcel_search.descriptor.json guards.entitlement `"product": "parcel_tool"` — the same file's notes state "`guards.entitlement.product` is `lead_gen`" and that "Recording anything else here would make this descriptor lie", and programme.product_questions[0] repeats it, so the field contradicts its own evidence — set the field to `lead_gen` or delete the notes paragraph and the product question's premise.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile_parcel_search.descriptor.json config.why "The six page settings of the phone search and semi pages are REGISTERED logic variables ... debounce_ms, min_query_len, entitlement_stale_ms, lookup_retry_max and lookup_stale_ms" — six is claimed but five keys are listed here and config.logic_variables holds five rows, the sixth (maxbld_page_continue_wait_ms) being declared only in the sibling semi descriptor — name the sixth key here or say five.

DEFER severity=MED — mobile_parcel_search.descriptor.json states `"name": "hit", "golden": "reports_left"` — the notes say "hit is renamed redirect (the screen navigates, it renders no hit)", so this entry is a dead state that goldens must still satisfy alongside `"name": "redirect"` — delete the hit entry and keep redirect.

DEFER severity=MED — contract_parcels_entitlement.descriptor.json limitations[0] `"check_id": "contract_parcels_entitlement__auth_class_parity"` — a limitation about `a11y.touch_target_min_px` is pinned to the auth-class parity check, so no check in checks[] actually covers the gap it escalates — cite an a11y or schema_declared check, or omit check_id.

DEFER severity=MED — mobile_parcel_search.descriptor.json emits.evidence "mobile/app/(app)/parcel-tool/index.tsx:1-115" — the no track() call proof is scoped to line 115 while evidence.emits cites ":1-312" and checks cite ":287, :297, :304" in the same file, so the proof does not cover the lines the rest of the descriptor rests on — widen the range to the whole file.

DEFER severity=LOW — mobile_parcel_search.descriptor.json docs.under_126 "both externalised in `mobile/src/constants/parcelSearch.ts`" — config.evidence says the same two values are "SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS and SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LEN read from the slice through sliceNumber" at "SearchBinding.tsx:37-38", so two files are named as the owner of one constant — name a single owner ("cannot see" which is right).
